item.title: North Carolina owner wins appeal over city's immunity defence in 361-home flooding dispute
item.description: A North Carolina property owner has won a significant legal victory against the City of Concord in her lawsuit. This case involves stormwater flooding allegedly caused by a nearby residential development, leading to property damage. The North Carolina Court of Appeals ruled that the city cannot claim governmental immunity at this stage. The decision allows the property owner to continue her claims of negligence, trespass, and nuisance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A retired architect in Dicmo, Croatia, spent nearly 50 years collecting carved stones from his family’s land, and archaeologists now say they belonged to a lost 1,900-year-old Roman arch built for Trajan
item.description: Archaeological excavations in Dicmo, Croatia, have revealed a stunning Roman triumphal arch dedicated to Emperor Trajan, believed to have stood for nearly 1,900 years. Božo Kokan's efforts in gathering stones from his relatives' land played a pivotal role in identifying this significant find. The site boasts intricate Roman architectural features and elements like the imperial eagle, along with signs of a larger Roman community, underscoring the area’s extensive historical narrative.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: At least 36 trains robbed; 14 accused in $22.5 million Nike cargo theft racket in US
item.description: Fourteen people have been indicted in the US for allegedly stealing over $22.5 million worth of cargo from at least 36 freight trains in Southern California. The stolen goods included Nike sneakers and Milwaukee tools, which were allegedly resold on the black market. Investigators claim the gang used social media to coordinate thefts and sales.

item.title: Begg Receives Tusk Honour: Begg becomes first woman to win; Niassa teams gain recognition
item.description: Dr. Colleen Begg has received the prestigious 2026 Prince William Award for Conservation in Africa, reflecting her commitment to safeguarding wildlife in Mozambique's Niassa Special Reserve. For over twenty years, she has worked alongside her husband to establish the Niassa Carnivore Project, focusing on large carnivore conservation through community engagement. This accolade underscores the vital role of sustainable practices and local leadership in conservation efforts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California 'lost shark guy', 68, names 56 species, hunts fish unseen since 1926
item.description: For decades, marine biologist David Ebert has journeyed to fish markets worldwide, uncovering the mysteries of sharks and rays. His remarkable contributions include documenting 56 new species, revealing the astonishing diversity of marine life. Ebert passionately advocates for recognizing the neglected shark species, underlining the integral role they play in maintaining healthy ocean ecosystems and the threats they face from human activities.

item.title: Jensen Huang told one employee his mother should have aborted him; yelled at another that he would remove the top of their head and urinate on their brain: NYT investigation
item.description: Jensen Huang believed that his bullying had entertainmet value and it was practice inflicted on newcomers to test their resilience as to whether they could withstand Huang's episodes of public humiliation. item.title: US Senate passes energy bill requiring AI data centres to pay more for grid upgrades
item.description: The US Senate has passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, designed to bolster energy infrastructure significantly. This new law mandates that large AI data centers play a larger role in funding electricity grid improvements. Environmental advocates raise alarms over potential threats to regulatory controls and tribal rights.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ohio court overturns divorce deal after husband alleges wife hid $443,000 in personal spending
item.description: An Ohio businessman, Jason G. Jardine, successfully appealed a divorce settlement ruling due to undisclosed expenditures by his ex-wife, Crystal T. Jardine. The Ohio Court of Appeals determined that the original decision lacked a hearing concerning fraud allegations. Jason claimed Crystal obtained significant undocumented funds during their divorce, complicating their dispute over funeral home management and associated receiver fees. The court has mandated further hearings to address these financial matters.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Dog helps find missing owner, alerts lodge staff; rescuers find 69-year-old alive after freezing night
item.description: Becky, the brave Basset hound, made her unexpected debut at a mountain lodge, alone and worried. Staff were quick to act, involving rescue teams equipped with drones and bloodhounds in the search for her missing owner. After enduring a frostbite-inducing night in the wilderness, he was located thanks to his loyal companion's timely arrival. Without Becky leading the way, the outcome could have been much grimmer for him.

item.title: Mamdani unveils $290m plan to close Rikers Island by 2032, five years past legal deadline
item.description: In a bold move, New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has unveiled a strategic initiative aimed at closing Rikers Island jail by 2032. The plan emphasizes the establishment of four smaller jails across various boroughs, with a focus on slashing the jail population. Key investments in mental health services and job training are central to this effort, as the city seeks to reform the beleaguered jail system.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Arizona toddler, 2, wanders into desert wearing only a diaper; volunteer finds her alive under bush
item.description: A two-year-old girl named Vella Campillo vanished from her home in Eloy, Arizona, prompting an extensive search by volunteers and officials in the chilly desert for several hours. After more than five hours of searching, neighbor Jay Stewart found her hiding under a bush. Emergency responders ensured the girl's safety and promptly took her to a hospital for evaluation. Authorities classified this incident as a case of a wandering child.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida mom buys 480 toilet paper rolls, earns miles for daughter's flight home
item.description: In an effort to minimize travel costs, Florida resident Michelle Jolene bought toilet paper through an airline shopping website, amassing 8,500 airline miles. These miles allowed her daughter to fly home for Thanksgiving from Washington, D.C. As airfares continue to climb, families face challenges with ticket prices and possible cancellations during the holiday rush. Michelle's inventive method showcases the potential for everyday spending to alleviate travel expenses.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mississippi politician's Nike sneaker idea expands nationwide for 2027 high school valedictorians
item.description: Nike has announced plans to reward high school valedictorians with custom Air Force 1 sneakers across the United States. This initiative originated from a request by incoming Mississippi senator Scott Colom to honor state valedictorians. Following Colom's appeal, Nike decided to expand the program to include all eligible students nationwide. Colom also suggested that the sneakers could feature historical figure Hiram Revels to connect education and Mississippi's history.
